title: Calculating back wages after reinstatement - the common disputes
p1:
An employee wins reinstatement after an unfair termination. Does that automatically mean they get every month’s salary they missed?

Many people assume the answer is yes. But back wages often become the biggest point of disagreement after reinstatement.
p2:
The surprising part is that reinstatement and back wages are not always the same thing. Courts may consider factors like whether the employee worked elsewhere during the period, how long the dispute lasted, and the circumstances of the termination.

For example, an employee may be reinstated but receive reduced back wages if the situation does not justify full payment.
p3:
The real dispute is usually not about returning to the job. It is about calculating what compensation is fair for the lost period.

A practical takeaway: reinstatement restores employment, but back wages require a separate evaluation based on facts, not assumptions.
conclusion: Have you seen cases where an employee was reinstated but did not receive full back wages? What factors do you think should decide the amount?
